item.title: [222] >all future game releases will undoubtedly contain some degree of AI Maybe I'm
item.description:
>all future game releases will undoubtedly contain some degree of AI
Maybe I'm just an oldhead and need to get with the times, but it was nice living in a time where you knew for sure that a video game was 100% crafted with human input
There's something icky about the knowledge that developers have unlimited access to a technology that basically strips this away, and there's no way to audit the fact it was used, especially for coding purposes
Like if I'm buying a video game, I'd expect it to be made with intentional design choices and hand crafted assets
But with all the stigma surrounding AI, it's only going to lead more and more game devs to disguise the fact that AI was used

item.title: [218] LANTERNS Writers Double Down on Hal Jordan’s Racism, Can’t Understand Complaints
item.description:
>"The thing that has been very, very shocking to me was the inability to have some nuance about Hal's portrayal," writer Vanessa Baden Kelly said of the reaction from fans. "I'm from Florida, so I grew up around a lot of white people who would probably use the N-word amongst their peers and then also turn around and defend you in something."

>"I can look at Hal's microaggressions and be like, yeah, he's got some racist tendencies because he's a man of a certain age that grew up in a certain time and place," Kelly continued. "I also feel like he probably fucks aliens in other places and doesn't feel like he's non-discriminatory."

>"And both things are true. For the audiences to sometimes not be able to hold that both things are true was really difficult for me, because they're like, 'Why are you making him a racist?'" she added. "Like, no, I'm making him a 60-year-old dude. I think that he is in the way that 60-year-old white dudes from the South can be, but don't think they are because they golf with a Black dude."

>Kelly and fellow writer Justin Britt-Gibson went on to Hal and John's dynamic to that of Joe Biden and Kamala Harris. As Britt-Gibson puts it, "you've been holding on to this sort of legacy, and then all of a sudden this guy comes around, young and Black and handsome, and strong and confident. It's threatening."

>Later, Kelly explained how Aaron Pierre's lighter skin tone changed how they wrote the show and implied that the Guardians of the Universe were more open to choosing John because his skin wasn't as dark as that of his brothers. "Justin and I baked in this idea that part of his being chosen is because they felt like his particular looks were more palatable to white people."

item.title: [ 32] Was Clayton retarded?
item.description:
He seems incredibly short-sighted for a character who was supposed to be an experienced hunter.

For one thing, he doesn't seem to make any efforts to actually find the gorilla nesting grounds himself, even though it should be abundantly clear that the location must be within a reasonable walking distance since Tarzan goes between there and the human camp fairly quickly. Instead he just demands that Tarzan tell him where the gorillas are. As a hunter, shouldn't he have a lot of experience in tracking animals on his own?

Secondly, he makes a massive mistake before the climax of the film. Why didn't he just let the Porters and Tarzan go off to England on the ship? They wouldn't have even been a problem then. As soon as the ship was gone and out of sight, the poachers and Clayton could have had free reign over the jungle and captured all the gorillas they wanted, then they'd just have to wait until a ship returned to collect them, and go home and sell all of them off for a large profit. He already had a map of where the nesting grounds were. He just had to be a little bit more patient.

item.title: [ 50] MAGA senator suffers embarrassing blunder while trying to defame Jack Smith in hearing
item.description:
Right Wing Law: Every accusation they make is a confession

https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senator-eric-schmitt-jack-smith-basketball-perjury-rcna600546

His slam dunk was a brick.

Sen. Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., accused former special counsel Jack Smith on Tuesday of committing perjury when he denied having attended a specific Atlanta Hawks basketball game in 2024 — to Smith’s apparent confusion.

The attempted trick play happened during a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on Smith’s now-scuttled investigations into President Donald Trump. But it soon emerged that Schmitt had the wrong team.

“Did you go to an NBA game between the Golden State Warriors and the Atlanta Hawks on Feb. 3, 2024?” Schmitt asked.

“What city would that be in?” a confused-looking Smith replied.

“Atlanta,” Schmitt responded.

“No,” Smith responded.

Schmitt pressed him again about whether he was in Atlanta on that date and then said he’d give him some “context” — it was the day after Fani Willis, the district attorney of Fulton County, Georgia, “came clean” about her romantic relationship with a prosecutor in her then-pending criminal case against Trump.

“The next day were you in Atlanta?” Schmitt continued.

“I do not believe so,” Smith responded. “I definitely did not go to a Hawks game. I’m sure of that.”
Schmitt then asked whether he ever met with the local prosecutors in Atlanta who charged Trump. “No,” Smith said.

“What would you say if I had a series of text messages from your team that said you were in Atlanta, at a Warrior-Hawks game, on Feb. 3, 2024, the day after Willis and [Nathan] Wade announced their affair?” Schmitt continued as a staffer held up a poster board that had three text messages about Smith’s going to an event.

The staffer quickly took the poster down as Smith looked on, appearing confused.

“I don’t think you know that we have this stuff, so I’ll give you a second to process it so you don’t perjure yourself,” Schmitt said.

item.title: [ 50] Trump Is Finally Admitting His War Against Iran Is Not Over And He Has Not Won It
item.description:
The concession comes after months of claiming the exact opposite.

https://www.huffpost.com/entry/trump-iran-war-not-over_n_6ababc2ee4b0cdca1abdc2fa

WASHINGTON ― After having claimed dozens of times during the spring and summer that his war against Iran was effectively over and that he had won it, President Donald Trump is now admitting that neither assertion was true.

For the second time in as many days, Trump on Monday said his war that began seven months ago today is still ongoing. “We’re going to win that war very soon,” he told reporters during an Oval Office photo opportunity.

The message was the same the day previous, in an interview with Fox News during his visit to a golf tournament outside Chicago. “I think what’s going to happen is we’re going to win the war very soon,” he said.

The statements come after the several dozens of times in recent months that Trump has claimed the war was essentially already over. They reflect a new effort by Trump and the GOP to convince angry midterm election voters that the war ― and the price hikes that have accompanied it ― will end soon.

“Let me tell you, we’ve won. You know, you never like to say too early you won. We won. We won the ― in the first hour, it was over,” he bragged at a March 11 rally in Kentucky.

On numerous other occasions, Trump has said a peace deal was days or even hours away, or that he could secure such an agreement because Iran was “begging” for one.

“They’re willing to give us everything,” he said at a June 8 speech in South Carolina, in which he also claimed he would “declare total victory” in the next two weeks.

Trump’s White House did not respond to HuffPost queries asking why the president was now changing his analysis about the war and who had won it.

item.description:
Media commentators in the MAGA movement shredded Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders on Monday over a new TV ad depicting white male gamers as the target of a state welfare fraud crackdown — and claimed the Republican hadn't injected enough race into her messaging.

Drawing the ire of the right: Sanders' promotion of new work requirements for Natural State welfare recipients, featuring a tousle-headed gamer named "Brad," shown in the advert mashing a video game controller and scarfing potato chips.

"Brad has turned relaxing into a full-time profession," Sanders tells voters in the ad. "But you, you actually work hard. You pay taxes to cover welfare for guys like Brad who just choose not to work."

Republicans and conservatives eyeing greater restrictions on welfare recipients have repeatedly invoked the image of a gamer, typically young and male, when speaking about Americans they say abuse government benefits. But Sanders' cheese ball-munching "Brad" proved especially offensive to far-right commentators.

The dustup targeting Sanders, a longtime Trump loyalist and former White House press secretary during his first term, illustrates how achieving long-standing conservative policy goals — like work requirements for government aid recipients — is often not enough for identity-obsessed MAGA allies, who want to display dominance over their perceived political enemies far more than they want to fix the nuts and bolts of governance.

Conservative podcast host Matt Walsh claimed the number of single white men on welfare was "minuscule" and "practically non-existent."

"Meanwhile, back in reality, women are significantly more likely to be on welfare than men," Walsh fumed in a reply to Sanders posted to twitter. "And black people are astronomically more likely to be on welfare than white people."

If they flip the House, Democrats say they’re ready to confront Israel on human rights.

The issue has long challenged the party, pitting staunch Israel defenders against more liberal lawmakers critical of Israel’s treatment of Palestinians. Democratic leaders have taken pains to avoid legislation that might highlight those divisions.

But heading into the midterms, when Democrats are expected to win control of the lower chamber, party leaders now say they’re preparing to confront head-on Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s prime minister, when it comes to Palestinian autonomy and broader issues of human rights.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.), who’s in line to become Speaker if the House changes hands, is pointing to one area in particular that Democrats intend to tackle: the rise of settler violence in the West Bank.

item.title: [ 61] A past FBI inquiry complicates Susan Collins’s campaign message in Maine
item.description:
https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/09/26/an-fbi-inquiry-complicates-susan-collinss-campaign-message-maine/

BATH, Maine — For two decades, the sprawling warehouses and work yards of Bath Iron Works have served as the backdrop for Susan Collins’s political campaigns. Her message to voters: As Maine’s senior senator, she brings jobs and money to the people of Bath.

This month, Collins appeared at that same shipyard, shaking hands with some of the 6,000 workers who assemble vessels for the U.S. Navy.

Before she departed, a group of workers delivered her a letter, signed by over 100 employees, thanking her for her work in Washington. As a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, she has helped secure more than $10 billion in Navy contracts for the yard since 2020, according to her office.

Now, as Collins faces a tight reelection race against Democrat Troy Jackson, allegations involving a different defense contractor are putting her broader record of steering money to Maine under scrutiny and raising a politically charged question: Where does Collins’s aggressive advocacy on behalf of Mainers end and improper influence begin?

This week, the nonprofit newsroom ProPublica disclosed that FBI agents had examined allegations that campaign contributions benefiting Collins were connected to federal contracts sought by a Hawaii-based defense company.

item.title: [ 63] Washington Taxed Its Millionaires. Now the Rich Want It Repealed.
item.description:
https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/27/us/politics/washington-state-millionaires-tax.html

Voters in Washington State will soon be asked to decide which they resent more: rich people or new taxes.

At issue is the state’s new “millionaires tax,” a 9.9 percent tax on income over $1 million a year that is expected to bring in more than $3 billion annually and, in the process, ease if not solve the state’s ongoing fiscal problems.

Critics want voters to repeal it and bar state leaders from imposing income taxes in the future, arguing the millionaires tax will drive out wealthy entrepreneurs and eventually lead to income taxes on everyone else.

“The goal is to put an income tax on every Washingtonian,” former United States Representative Jaime Herrera Beutler, a Republican, said at a recent news conference organized by one of the campaigns working to repeal the tax. “Don’t let them fool you.”

The November election will test how voters feel about taxing the rich up and down the West Coast. In California, voters are considering both a “millionaire tax” and a “billionaire tax.” The less debated proposal asks voters to make permanent a temporary income tax hike on couples who earn at least $743,000 a year.

Voters will also decide whether to approve a new wealth tax on people with at least $1 billion in assets, a proposal that has generated enormous blowback from wealthy residents as well as teachers and health care interests who fear it will damage the state budget.

item.title: [ 82] A Trump 2024 Campaign Ad Returns, Now Brought to You by the Government
item.description:
https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/27/us/politics/trump-ad-government-campaign.html

As President Trump ran to return to the White House in 2024, his campaign released a somber, black-and-white ad in which he railed against the “deep state” and vowed to expel “warmongers” from government.

“This is the final battle,” Mr. Trump is heard saying in the online ad, which shows him walking silently down a hallway.

That ad has returned this weekend, airing on television stations across the country, with one notable difference: As it ends, the words “Paid for by the U.S. Government” appear on the screen.

The spot is the latest in a series of pro-Trump ads funded by public money. Some ethics experts have argued that the Trump administration is violating federal laws banning the use of taxpayer dollars for propaganda, and the ads have drawn criticism from both parties. The most recent ad, one expert argued, is a more flagrant violation given its prior use in the political arena.

“The president and his administration have gone from breaking the law to trampling it,” said Norm Eisen, a former White House special counsel for ethics and government reform under Barack Obama, who has sued the Trump administration several times. “The prior ad was bad enough, but this one openly repurposes prior political conduct.”

item.title: [ 58] The Supreme Court revives a controversial data system for citizenship checks
item.description:
https://www.npr.org/2026/09/25/nx-s1-5976804/supreme-court-trump-save-noncitizen-voting

The U.S. Supreme Court has for now revived a federal data system the Department of Homeland Security revamped into a tool to check the citizenship of millions of Americans on state voter rolls. The tool has mistakenly flagged some eligible voters as potential noncitizens.

The news comes as the Trump administration has been pouring resources into searching for noncitizens on voter rolls ahead of the upcoming election.

Many states uploaded their voter lists to the expanded version of the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements data system — known as SAVE — sharing that voter information with the federal government. Tens of millions of voter records were run through SAVE before it was blocked by a federal judge in Washington, D.C., in June.

The Supreme Court's decision clears the way for the administration to again use the revamped SAVE in its hunt for noncitizens on voter rolls, as well as in its unprecedented project of compiling lists of adult citizens in each state.

Any impact on the midterm elections is unclear. Federal law bans states from "systematically" removing voters from rolls within 90 days of a federal election.

The Trump administration and Republican state officials have made the case that the statute should not apply to removing noncitizens who were improperly registered. And the federal government argued to the Supreme Court that at a minimum, the updated SAVE should be able to be used for individual removal decisions ahead of an election.

item.title: [135] USA travel cont'd: tripping thru Texas addition
item.description:
Say hi to the friendly neighbor dog who up and joined me on an LSD-infused four mile stroll through the 95° sunshine and greenery of east Texas in August. Pretty comfy desu, it's lovely to never be cold. Humidity is moderate compared to Southeast Asia, doesn't bother me at all.

Tomorrow me and my brother drive across the state to repo his car from his ex fiance. The roadtrip is going to kickstart the next episode of adventures across America, with an eight-day itinerary stopping at various Deep South cities on my way to the East Coast.

Despite poison ivy and blisters from yard projects, it felt good to have a house to relax in deep in the unvisited countryside of east Texas. But after a week here, I'm eager to get a move on and bask in the warmth of a southern summertime while traversing some very black ghettoish places. Got a couple tabs left over for my next fraternal reunion on the East Coast...this is the life. Own nothing, be happy. Overseas to home country without missing a beat, keep it moving, spend that cash, don't let it rot in the bank. Some other anon said $5K is his return-to-work threshold. Good idea. Enjoy the fruits of your labor while you can; health and freedom are temporal privileges which Fate can revoke any minute.

Would be nice to take this all the way up to Quebec and the Maritimes before summer wraps up. We'll see how far it goes.
